summary: Premier Properties of New Brunswick is a New Brunswick-only developer/manager of new-construction rental buildings aimed mainly at Rutgers students and their parents, with roughly 350 units under management across about a dozen downtown addresses and studio-to-three-bedroom rents of $1,210-$4,200/month. Its leasing front door is a phone call: the pricing page says 'CALL FOR DETAILS', the contact form has no phone field, and tours are only offered at seasonal open houses or after an applicant comes to the office and qualifies. A single Leasing Assistant posting ($22/hr) bundles prospect calls, applications, tours, maintenance work orders and deposit collection, which is where the manual load concentrates.

facts.fact: Company states it has over 25 years of experience, is one of the city's largest rental development and management operations, and operates ONLY in the City of New Brunswick.

A 2022 NJBIZ profile reprinted on the company's own site says Premier Properties has approximately 350 housing units under management in New Brunswick, while affiliate Construction Management Associates has built or developed more than 500 units there.

The pricing page lists about a dozen buildings with per-unit rents from $1,210 (jr. studio, 276 Hamilton St) to $4,200 (three-bedroom, 191 Hamilton St), most dated 'Available June 1, 2027', under the banner 'Now Leasing for the Spring Semester' and 'CALL FOR DETAILS'.
All rents exclude utilities; tenants open their own PSE&G account, water is a flat monthly charge that varies by building, no pets, and leases are 12 months.

Tours are restricted: the company holds open houses in the fall and spring, and otherwise 'we do not show apartments to anyone unless they come to the office and qualify first', except for units advertised as immediately available.

Applying does not hold a unit - 'only a completed lease guarantees a spot'; there is also a Preferred Tenants List requiring an application, W-9, Preferred Tenant Agreement and a $500 refundable deposit.

The contact page offers only a four-field form (first name, last name, email, message) plus office phone (732) 246-7048 and generalmanager@premiernb.com; address 205 Easton Ave, New Brunswick, NJ 08901; hours M-F 9:00 AM-5:00 PM.

Google Maps profile shows 'Premier Properties of New Brunswick: Rutgers Off Campus Housing', 4.5 stars, category 'Property management company', 205 Easton Ave Apt 1, closed with 'Opens 9 AM Mon', phone (732) 246-7048, site premiernb.com.

Birdeye's mirror of the Google listing shows 4.0 stars from 102 reviews, with the rating split 70 five-star, 6 four-star, 2 three-star, 6 two-star and 18 one-star, and the profile marked 'not claimed by the business owner'.
A 'Leasing Assistant - (1 year experience)' posting for the company ran at $22/hr, full-time onsite Monday-Friday, posted Sep 24, 2026, updated Oct 27, 2026, and is now expired/unavailable.
The site footer carries 'Powered by AppFolio Property Manager', and the resident portal handles online rent payment and maintenance requests.

New Brunswick's zoning board approved a 150-unit, $60 million Union Square project at 40/46/50 Union Street from 50 Union Street Realty LLC, a subsidiary of Construction Management Associates and Premier Properties; co-founder Mitchell Broder told the board construction would likely begin within 'a few years'.

191 Hamilton Street is described as the newest building with garage parking, elevator, fitness room, Amazon Hub, common lounge and two 2,200 sq ft outdoor terraces; construction there began September 2017.
At a 390 px viewport the site still lays out at 768 px (document scrollWidth 768), so navigation and form fields are clipped off-screen; the site's CSS sets min-width 768px on the page wrapper.

operations_signals: Availability is phone-gated: the pricing list headlines 'CALL FOR DETAILS' under 'Now Leasing for the Spring Semester', so every price/availability question becomes a staff call (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/pricing-list)

The only written enquiry path is a contact form with first name, last name, email and message - no phone field, no unit-of-interest field, no move-in date - guaranteeing an email round trip before anyone can call back (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/contact-us)

Office hours are M-F 9:00 AM-5:00 PM, closed Saturday and Sunday, while the audience is students and out-of-state parents who often search evenings and weekends; Google shows 'Closed - Opens 9 AM Mon' (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/location-map)

Tours are deliberately limited - seasonal open houses only, otherwise an in-office qualification step first - and there is no online tour scheduler or application anywhere on the site (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/faq)

Leasing paperwork (application, W-9, Preferred Tenant Agreement, $500 deposit; electronic lease signing) is handled manually per prospect, including a program for out-of-state and foreign renters who cannot visit (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/about-us)

Existing residents self-serve through the AppFolio-powered portal for rent payment and maintenance requests, so the manual load sits on the prospect side (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/tenant/tenant-portal)
Leases run 12 months with most starting June 1 or September 1, so nearly the entire portfolio re-leases in two annual waves (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/about-us)
There is no careers page - /careers returns HTTP 404 - so hiring runs entirely through third-party boards (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/careers)
The office inbox is a role address (generalmanager@premiernb.com) rather than a named person, and all site contact routes funnel there (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/contact-us)
hiring_signals: Leasing Assistant, $22/hr, full-time onsite Mon-Fri, posted Sep 24 2026 and last updated Oct 27 2026; the listing is now expired, suggesting a replacement or backfill cycle rather than growth hiring (https://tallo.com/talent/job/hospitality/concierge/nj/new-brunswick/leasing-assistant-1-year-ex-8216cd26)

The same posting's duties bundle answering incoming calls from prospective tenants, administrative work, processing lease applications/credit reports/renewals, scheduling and conducting unit tours, property inspections and turnovers, maintenance calls and work orders, and security-deposit and rent collection for new residents - one seat absorbing intake, admin and collections (https://tallo.com/talent/job/hospitality/concierge/nj/new-brunswick/leasing-assistant-1-year-ex-8216cd26)

The posting requires availability over Memorial Day weekend, consistent with the late-May/June 1 lease-start crunch (https://tallo.com/talent/job/hospitality/concierge/nj/new-brunswick/leasing-assistant-1-year-ex-8216cd26)
No current openings are published on the company's own site (no careers page), so hiring demand is only visible on aggregators (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/careers)
review_themes: Two public listings disagree on the headline number: Google Maps shows 4.5 stars, while Birdeye's mirror of the Google listing shows 4.0 from 102 reviews - either way the volume is meaningful for a ~350-unit manager (https://reviews.birdeye.com/premier-properties-of-new-brunswick-rutgers-off-campus-housing-164556339877922)

The Birdeye rating distribution is sharply bimodal - 70 five-star against 18 one-star - which reads as strong enthusiasm for some interactions and hard failures in others rather than uniform mediocrity (https://reviews.birdeye.com/premier-properties-of-new-brunswick-rutgers-off-campus-housing-164556339877922)

Praise in aggregator summaries centres on maintenance speed and clean, secure buildings (e.g. a water-heater repair handled same hour); these summaries were read via search results, not the review text itself (https://reviews.birdeye.com/premier-properties-of-new-brunswick-rutgers-off-campus-housing-164556339877922)

A 2022 r/rutgers tenant thread, as summarised in search results, praises fast maintenance and prompt answers but flags thin walls, limited tour windows and a 48-hour lease-signing deadline; the thread itself was not readable (https://www.reddit.com/r/rutgers/comments/tp8hjv)

The listing is unclaimed on Birdeye and no review widget appears on the company's own site, so 100+ reviews of social proof are invisible to visitors at the point of decision (https://reviews.birdeye.com/premier-properties-of-new-brunswick-rutgers-off-campus-housing-164556339877922)
tech_footprint: Property management and portal software is AppFolio - the site footer carries the 'Powered by AppFolio Property Manager' badge and the resident portal is the AppFolio tenant login (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/location-map)

Website is built on Duda (cdn-website.com asset host, dmAPI runtime, dmform widgets) - inference from the page source fingerprints, not a vendor statement (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/)

No online booking, tour scheduling or rental application exists; the only conversion paths are a phone number, a mailto address and a four-field form (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/contact-us)
The public site still shows '© 2022 All Rights Reserved' in the footer despite content being updated for 2026-2027 availability dates (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/pricing-list)
The /management-services page is still lorem ipsum placeholder text - a live, linked page with no real content (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/management-services)

Floor plans are published only as images (JPGs of plan drawings), so prices, square footage and unit numbers are not structured data; a sitemap.xml and robots.txt exist (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/property/191-hamilton-street)
Social presence is Facebook and Instagram (facebook.com/premiernb, instagram.com/premiernb) linked from the footer only (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/contact-us)
growth_signals: Union Square at 40/46/50 Union Street was approved in February 2023 as a 150-unit, $60 million building with a 1,300 sq ft fitness room, 3,000 sq ft of lounges, 67 parking spaces and rooftop solar - roughly a 40% increase on the ~350 units currently managed (https://jerseydigs.com/union-square-new-brunswick/)

191 Hamilton Street is presented as the newest addition, with construction started September 2017 and a 'Watch Us Grow' page tracking its progress (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/watch-us-grow)

The 2026-2027 availability list is dominated by June 1, 2027 move-ins plus a January 4, 2027 tranche, i.e. the company is already pre-leasing the next two academic cycles (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/pricing-list)

The portfolio has expanded beyond students into a 55-and-older property at 76 Louis Street and into hospital-adjacent midtown addresses near Robert Wood Johnson and St. Peter's (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/about-us)
Press page aggregates coverage including an NJBIZ profile and a 'Top 5 Little City in America' piece, used as marketing proof (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/)
physical_signals: About a dozen managed addresses in two clusters: Easton Ave, Union St, Mine St and Sicard St next to the Rutgers College Ave campus, and Hamilton, Maple and Louis St 'midtown' (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/pricing-list)

Named buildings include 191 Hamilton St, 276 Hamilton St ('The Mansion'), 6 Sicard St, 15/32/40/50 Union St, 17 Mine St, 15 Maple St, 76 Louis St and 205 Easton Ave (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/pricing-list)

191 Hamilton Street: garage parking, elevator, fitness room, Amazon Hub package lockers, common lounge, two 2,200 sq ft outdoor terraces with grills and seating, and studio through three-bedroom plus duplex layouts (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/property/191-hamilton-street)

All properties are new construction with the oldest building from 1999, electronic entrance door locking, around-the-clock video surveillance, yearly-inspected sprinkler systems and weekly professional cleaning of common areas (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/about-us)
Every building has an in-building laundry facility; units are unfurnished and come with a basic appliance set, and no pets are allowed (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/faq)
76 Louis Street is an age-restricted 55-and-older property offering two-bedrooms, with free on-site parking at the midtown locations (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/about-us)
A single downtown office at 205 Easton Ave serves all buildings, described as centrally located so staff can be hands-on (https://www.premierpropertiesofnewbrunswick.com/location-map)
Roughly 350 units under management as of the August 2022 NJBIZ profile (https://irp.cdn-website.com/c93f6c1f/files/uploaded/NJBIZ.pdf)
decision_maker: Mitchell (Mitch) Broder, president and co-founder - named in the NJBIZ profile reprinted on the company's own site; co-founder Laszlo 'Les' Salamon runs construction/field operations via Construction Management Associates. No general manager is named publicly; the site publishes only generalmanager@premiernb.com (https://irp.cdn-website.com/c93f6c1f/files/uploaded/NJBIZ.pdf)

inferences.inference: Leasing response capacity, not demand, is the binding constraint.
inferences.reasoning: Every price/availability question routes to a phone call ('CALL FOR DETAILS'), the web form cannot capture a callable number, hours are M-F 9-5, and a single $22/hr Leasing Assistant posting carries prospect calls, applications, tours, work orders and collections - so after-hours and peak-season enquiries queue up.

inferences.inference: The 18 one-star reviews most likely cluster around leasing/communication and deposit friction rather than maintenance quality.
inferences.reasoning: Public praise themes centre on fast maintenance and clean buildings, while the documented pain points (restricted tours, short signing windows, unclaimed listing, no review engagement) sit in the leasing process; this is a reasoned guess because individual review text could not be read.

inferences.inference: The business has an unusually repetitive annual intake workload.
inferences.reasoning: Most of ~350 units run 12-month leases starting June 1 or September 1, so nearly the whole portfolio turns over in two waves that coincide with finals, graduations and out-of-state parents researching remotely.

inferences.inference: Non-responsive mobile layout is directly costly for this specific audience.
inferences.reasoning: The buyer is a student or parent searching on a phone; at 390 px the site renders 768 px wide with nav and form fields clipped, while competitors' listings on Apartments.com and similar portals are mobile-first.

inferences.inference: An agent could be wired into existing systems rather than replacing them.
inferences.reasoning: AppFolio already holds units, leases, payments and work orders, and all availability/pricing is already published as plain text on one page - so an intake/answering agent needs integration, not a data rebuild.

inferences.inference: Union Square will multiply administrative load before it multiplies headcount.
inferences.reasoning: A 150-unit addition on top of ~350 managed units adds roughly 40% more units and proportionally more leasing and work-order volume at turnover; the company's pattern is to hire one generalist assistant rather than build process.

data_gaps: Google review count was not visible in the limited Maps view (rating 4.5 displayed); individual Google review text could not be read, and Birdeye rendered only the rating distribution, not review bodies.
The 2022 r/rutgers thread was blocked/unreadable to direct fetching; its themes are reported from search-engine summaries and are four years old.
Indeed and Apartments.com returned HTTP 403, so their job counts and any renter reviews are unverified.
The New Brunswick zoning minutes PDF that reportedly sets 191 Hamilton St at 39 units / 45 garage spaces was surfaced in search but not opened, so per-building unit counts are not confirmed.
No employee headcount, revenue or ownership entity list is published; the ~350-unit figure is from an August 2022 press reprint.
Yelp and BBB were not read; no verified Yelp rating is reported here.
Only one job posting was found and it is expired as of Nov 2026; no currently open roles could be confirmed.
Could not confirm whether an online rental application exists behind the AppFolio portal (portal requires login, which was not attempted).
